label: A working-class parish in the city
blurb: Your grandparents' parish, in a neighborhood that has changed twice since they arrived. The church is too big for the people left in it.
outcome: You know the smell of a sacristy and the way a parish runs when the pastor is old and the secretary is really in charge. You can talk to a plumber and a widow in the same afternoon. What you do not have is the polish that suburban parishes mistake for competence. Your mother still lights a candle for you on Thursdays.

hooks.label: The parish you grew up in, half-empty now
A friend from the block who went a different way

label: A Latino immigrant family
blurb: Your parents came north with nothing but the faith and a phone number. Mass was in Spanish in the parish hall until the parish gave in and moved it to the church.
outcome: You are bilingual without ever having studied it, and you know what a parish looks like from the folding chairs at the back. Every Latino parish in the diocese will read you as one of theirs before you open your mouth; some of the others will not. Your mother assumes you will be a bishop. Your father has never said what he thinks.

hooks.label: The parish where the Spanish Mass was in the hall
Relatives in the old country who still expect money

label: A farm town
blurb: One parish for forty miles, a pastor who also had two mission churches, and a town that measured you by how early you got up.
outcome: You can fix things and you can wait. A rural parish will trust you the day you arrive; an urban one will take a year to decide you are not a hayseed. You have driven a hundred miles to Mass in weather that would keep a city man home, and you know what a parish looks like when there is no priest at all.

hooks.label: The one parish for forty miles
A farm that will need someone to take it or sell it

label: An affluent suburb
blurb: A parish with a school, a gym, and a pastor who golfed with the donors. Everyone assumed you would go to law school.
outcome: You are comfortable in a room of professionals and you read a budget without flinching. The suburban parishes will find you reassuring. The others will wonder what you are doing there and whether you will stay. Your parents were proud in the way people are proud of a surprising choice.

hooks.label: The parish with the gym and the golfing pastor
Friends who are making partner while you are in formation

label: A convert household
blurb: Your family came into the Church when you were a child, or you came alone as an adult. Either way, nothing about it was inherited.
outcome: You chose all of it, which means you can explain all of it, which cradle Catholics find either bracing or exhausting. You read more than the men around you and you have fewer instincts. You will be suspected of zeal for a long time, and sometimes the suspicion will be fair.

hooks.label: The parish where you were received
The church or the nothing you left, and the people still in it

label: A lapsed-Catholic family
blurb: Baptized, confirmed at your grandmother's insistence, and then nothing until something happened.
outcome: You came back on your own and you know exactly what it looks like from outside: the boredom, the half-remembered responses, the reasons people give for not returning. You can talk to the lapsed because you were one. Your family regards the whole thing as a phase that is going on too long.

hooks.label: The grandmother who insisted on your confirmation
Whatever it was that brought you back
